title: The Wave Hill walk-off

draft.title: The Wave Hill walk-off
card: In 1966 Gurindji stockmen, house workers and their families walked off Wave Hill station in the Northern Territory. Vincent Lingiari was their leader.
They protested about very low pay and poor living conditions. The station was owned by a British company, Vestey's.
The strike changed. The Gurindji began to ask for the return of part of their traditional land, Gurindji country, which they had cared for long before the station existed.
The campaign lasted years and drew wide public support. In 1975 Prime Minister Gough Whitlam handed back some of the land to the Gurindji, a landmark moment for land rights.
draft.remember: A strike over pay and conditions grew into a claim for land.

a.q: How did the aim of the Wave Hill walk-off change over time?
opts: From a protest about pay into a claim for land
From a claim for land into a protest about pay
From a protest about pay into a call for a new station
From a claim for land into a protest about housing
a.why: The workers first left over pay and conditions, then began asking for their traditional land to be returned. The change did not run the other way: land was not the first demand.
a.clue: Think about what the workers asked for first, and what they asked for later.

b.q: A student says the Wave Hill walk-off ended when the workers won better wages. Why is this wrong?
opts: The strike grew into a land claim that was met in 1975
The strike failed and the Gurindji gave up their claim
The strike was about land only and never about pay
The strike ended when the station owners closed Wave Hill
b.why: The protest began over pay and conditions but became a claim for land, and some land was returned in 1975. It is wrong to say it was only about land: pay and conditions were where it started.

a.best: From a protest about pay into a claim for land

b.best: The strike grew into a land claim that was met in 1975

problems.detail: 'A land claim that was met in 1975' suggests the claim was fully met. The card says Whitlam handed back only 'some of the land' in 1975. Wording such as 'partly met' or 'that led to land being returned in 1975' would match the card.

check.summary: The facts check out and both questions have one clear right answer. Question b's right option says the land claim was 'met' in 1975, which overstates the card's 'some of the land' and should be softened.

flags: Question b, wording: 'A land claim that was met in 1975' suggests the claim was fully met. The card says Whitlam handed back only 'some of the land' in 1975. Wording such as 'partly met' or 'that led to land being returned in 1975' would match the card.
